messages.author: d560d9e01924933c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA with survey data?
parts:
Thanks, I didn't know this paper.

I am actually using this approach, i.e. using the normalized sampling
weights scaling the log-likelihood, putting a prior and performing
some analysis in INLA and in MCMC as well.

There are some things that have to be in mind:

i) The weight argument should not for the sampling weights, as Havard
said it only scales the log-likelihood.
ii) In sampling literature, they do that, but they correct the
variance of the estimators. Since the weights could be very big, and
then the variances would be too small.
iii) This approach of using the sampling weights scaling the
log-likelihood is called Pseudo-likelihood, hence you no longer have a
posterior distribution, but a Pseudo posterior one.
iv) If you don't care about the pseudo-posterior, then it is fine use
the Vandendijck et al. paper. You may also read the Savitsty and Toth
paper on Pseudo-posteriors (
https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.ejs/1468847267 )
v) Last, but not least. There is no garantee that the pseudo-posterior
is actually a probability distribution. For some cases you are fine,
you can analytically derive the normalizing constant. But for other
scenarios there may be a prove that this constant is limited but I
don't know, therefore we may get invalid numerical results.

I am very interested in this stuff, and you be quite happy to
collaborate with anyone who is also interested in combining Bayesian
methods with sampling designs.

Cheers,
Leo

Sorry guys, the Vandendijck et al. paper. takes a different approach
then I thought. They do not use the weight argument in INLA, they deal
with the weights using Gaussian Process as suggested by Si et al.
(2015, Bayesian Analysis). This is a proper Bayesian approach. I
thought they were using the Pseudo-likelihood/Pseudo-posterior.

Thanks again for letting me know about this paper.

Cheers,
Leo

Thanks Dr. Rue for your reply. Also thanks for the paper. I got the chance to read it earlier. 

The main issue is, in my dataset, I have weight for each individual. Even your paper says that "The wij are known weights defined for each observed data points". 

The inla function is written in a way that if we had one single weight (say, 0.4583) assigned to all individuals in the data, it will do this, 

> rep(0.4583, dim(df)[1])

That way, all the individuals are receiving the same weight 0.4583. Since we have different weights for different individuals, so all the weights are being replicated. With my limited programming and statistical knowledge that's what I understood. 

Is there any way that inla will use only the assigned weights to each individuals while carrying out the analysis?

Thanks in advance. Really appreciate your effort.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA with survey data: throwing error
parts:
The new testing-version of today Version_18.02.14, accept argument
'weights' with family='coxph'.

this argument, will simply assign weight w[i] to datapoint i. since in
coxph, datapoint i is expanded into a poisson counts yy[j], yy[j+1],
..., yy[j+k], and all these poisson counts will inherit the weight of
the orgiginal datapoint, w[i].

If this is what you want, is something I cannot answer to...

Best
H
